learnings.title: Separate macro-release first reaction from later tape or close
learnings.claim: A high-impact macro release can trigger a knee-jerk cross-asset move that reverses later in the session; the first reaction must not be promoted to the session conclusion.
learnings.decision: For scheduled high-impact releases, store the official release value/time, then record T+initial reaction and T+later tape/close separately for 2Y/10Y, DXY, equities, gold and energy where available. Mark later observations as snapshots unless an official settlement/close source proves otherwise.
failure_history: Earlier Finance output treated the initial post-payroll yield/oil reaction as if it persisted through the session.
fallback_history: If later verified tape/close is unavailable, label the move initial reaction only and do not infer the close.
learnings.next_measurement: At the next high-impact release, capture official release time/value plus first reaction and later tape/close read-back.

learnings.title: Use Wolfram as the non-Python finance chart fallback
learnings.claim: Wolfram FinancialData and DateListPlot can retrieve supported real financial time series and render an inline visual chart without Python.
learnings.decision: Before raising finance_chart_missing, try Wolfram. For supported symbols, retrieve real FinancialData, convert quantities to numeric values, verify at least two real observations, normalize each series as 100*value/value0 when Base-100 is required, and render with DateListPlot. For unsupported symbols, pass only externally verified dated points to DateListPlot. Never interpolate or invent missing observations.
failure_history: Finance repeatedly emitted AUTO_DETECTED_FAILURE: finance_chart_missing without attempting an available non-Python renderer.
fallback_history: If Wolfram has no data for the asset, use another verified source for the dated series and Wolfram only as renderer; if neither data nor renderer is available, fail closed.
learnings.next_measurement: Render each required Finance category chart through Wolfram and verify the visual output appears before PASS.

learnings.title: Separate physical export-flow recovery from shipping-security risk
learnings.claim: Middle East crude exports can recover to or above pre-war levels even while tanker attacks and Hormuz security risk increase; nominal closure/security headlines alone do not measure delivered crude supply.
learnings.decision: Track verified export-flow volumes and shipping-security incidents as separate variables. For oil/inflation analysis, require physical-flow confirmation before converting a Hormuz security headline into a supply-loss assumption; preserve tanker/navlun risk as a separate cost/risk-premium channel.
failure_history: Earlier Finance framing risked treating Hormuz political/security restrictions as equivalent to current physical export loss.
fallback_history: When direct shipping data are unavailable, mark physical-flow impact N/A rather than infer it from political statements.
learnings.next_measurement: Compare daily Middle East crude export flow, tanker incidents, Brent/WTI and refined-product flows on the next liquid session.
